articles.title: When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can influence user trust and decision-making through subtle linguistic cues, yet the behavioral effects of manipulative outputs remain poorly quantified. articles.summary: arXiv:2607.01730v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Liquid democracy lets voters either vote directly or delegate their voting power to another trusted participant. articles.title: AgentStripes: An Evidence-Graded Maturity Model for AI Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.18603v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Benchmarks report what an Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent can do on a task suite, but not whether one released version has been engineered with the controls that make it reliable, safe and observable, or how strongly that is shown. This paper proposes AgentStripes, an evidence-graded maturity model for AI agents.
